title: Graduated validation checkpoints for multi-arm split tests and pilot releases
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define an actionable, auditable milestone sequence for multi-arm split tests and pilot releases that balances validation rigor with time-to-decision. This ticket defines the checkpoints, metric thresholds, instrumentation requirements, and runbook snippets that Product, Eng, and SRE will use to authorize traffic ramps for experiments that touch the inference stack (model variant, routing policy, batching config, quantization profile).

Scope: Multi-arm randomized experiments and controlled pilot releases across hosted and Dedicated deployments. Not a full rollout playbook — this focuses on decision milestones from pilot -> graduated ramp -> full release. Includes both user-facing A/B tests and server-side performance experiments.

Milestone overview (phased):
- Pilot (smoke & safety): 0.5% - 1% traffic for 24-48h. Objective: detect glaring correctness/latency regressions and integration failures. Must pass synthetic canary synthetic checks and feature flags enabled.
- Validation ramp: 5% traffic for 72h - 7d. Objective: accumulate statistically meaningful signal for primary product metrics and infra SLOs. Introduce matched shadow comparisons for key paths.
- Stability expansion: 25% traffic for 7-14d. Objective: observe steady-state behavior over longer window; evaluate operational costs, scale characteristics, and edge-case regressions.
- Production ingress: 100% gated rollout with progressive traffic policy and continuous monitors. Only after release sign-off and post-mortem-free pilot windows.

Primary signals and thresholds (must instrument all):
- Safety regressions: increase in 5xx or inference error rate > 0.05 percentage points => automatic pause and page on-call.
- Latency: p95 increase relative to baseline <= 12% during Pilot; <= 10% during Validation ramp. Any sustained p99 regression > 25% triggers rollback.
- Cost per 1k tokens: delta <= 30% during validation unless PM approves for targeted experiment. Unexpected spikes > 2x triggers manual review.
- Quality: end-to-end user metric (CTR / completion rate / success signal depending on feature) must not degrade by more than 1.5% absolute (or a relative threshold of 5% if baseline low).
- Statistical significance: primary product metric should reach >= 80% statistical power or a 95% confidence interval exclude the MDE where practical. For infra metrics, use moving-window anomaly detection.

Instrumentation & observability checklist (required before Pilot start):
- Charted dashboards: experiment-traffic, model-metrics (token-rate, KV cache hit rate), latency percentiles, error traces, cost breakdown by model and quantization variant. Links below.
- Experiment tagging: all requests must include experiment_id and cohort_id propagated into logs and traces.
- Synthetic probes: end-to-end synthetic requests that cover critical prompt templates every 5 minutes.
- Shadow traffic capture: capture 100% of inference inputs for 24-72h during Validation ramp for offline comparison (privacy review required).
- Data retention: experiment logs retained for 90 days; aggregated metrics for 1 year for OKR reporting.

Decision process and sign-offs:
- Pilot approval: PM + Eng lead + SRE on-call sign-off after 24h smoke checks.
- Validation gate: PM + Data Science + Eng Performance owner sign-off based on metric dashboard and experiment report.
- Expansion sign-off: Product Director signs off; Legal/Compliance to review shadow data if customer data captured.

Automated rollback triggers (immediate):
- Fatal errors: any increase in core user-facing 5xx > 0.5 percentage points within a 15 minute window.
- Latency spike p99 > 3x baseline for >= 10 minutes.
- Cost runaway: cost per token > 3x baseline sustained for 1 hour.
- Unexpected content-safety hits above configured thresholds.

Manual rollback triggers: sustained negative impact to retention/engagement beyond thresholds for 24h, or high-severity incidents uncovered in logs.

Post-pilot deliverables (within 5 business days):
- Experiment write-up: hypotheses, data slices, conf intervals, artifact links. Owner: experiment PM.
- Performance runbook updates: Eng to capture bottlenecks and mitigations.
- Small retrospective: 30-60 minute sync with Product/Eng/SRE.

Risk mitigations and trade-offs:
- To reduce false positives in infra signals we use paired rolling windows and shadow baselines. This increases analysis complexity but avoids premature rollbacks.
- Privacy: shadow-capture must be filtered to remove PII; consult Security. This may limit certain offline quality checks.
- Time to decision vs power: for very small user-impact metrics we accept lower power (50-60%) during Validation ramp and extend windows in Stability expansion.

Next steps (this ticket):

- Add experiment tagging middleware PR (ENG-38921) and measurement changes (ENG-39210).
- Pilot checklist QA and dry-run with synthetic traffic on staging by 2026-01-08.

Longer-term follow-ups (captured as child tasks):
- Consolidate experiment registry and auto-generated rollup reports (PM epic).
- Integrate OKR-level experiment reporting for quarterly reviews.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Playbook document checked into Confluence and linked here.
- Dashboards created and accessible to cross-functional team.
- Measurement PRs merged and experiment-tagging released to staging.

Notes: This roadmap intentionally separates safety checks (fast, strict) from statistical validation (slower, more nuanced). The thresholds above are recommendations and should be tuned per-experiment depending on user impact and traffic slices.
